paper_a.title: Making Gradient Descent Optimal for Strongly Convex Stochastic Optimization

metadata.description: Paper A analyses convergence rates of stochastic gradient descent for strongly convex stochastic optimization (last-iterate, average, suffix-average; upper and lower bounds of order 1/T or log T/T). Paper B introduces Flow Matching, a simulation-free regression objective for training continuous normalizing flows by matching a neural vector field to a (conditional) target vector field that generates a probability density path. Despite both involving gradients in some surface sense (SGD updates vs gradient of a regression loss in CNF training), the problems, mathematical objects (convex functions on R^d under noisy subgradient oracles vs probability density paths and time-dependent vector fields under the continuity equation), techniques (martingale concentration, projection inequalities, induction on 1/t recurrences vs Leibniz rule for the marginal-VF identity, OT/diffusion path constructions), and theorems are entirely disjoint. No paper-A node aligns with any paper-B node beyond a shared but uninformative use of generic gradient/stochastic-sampling vocabulary.

matches.explanation: Paper A's central problem is minimising a lambda-strongly convex function F over a convex domain via T noisy subgradient queries and bounding F(w_T)-F(w*). Paper B has no convex-optimisation-oracle problem; its problem (ProbP13.1) is simulation-free training of a CNF to push a prior to a data distribution. The two problems share no objects (no F, no w*, no oracle, no convex domain in B; no probability path, no vector field, no data distribution in A).

lambda-strong convexity of a scalar objective F has no analogue in paper B, which never assumes or uses convexity of any function. The closest concepts in B (e.g. Gaussian densities, OT displacement) are unrelated.
mu-smoothness of F with respect to the optimum w* is an objective-function regularity condition with no counterpart in paper B.

Polyak-Ruppert averaging of SGD iterates has no counterpart in flow matching, which has no iterates to average; CNF training optimises parameters theta of a neural vector field via standard gradient descent on a regression loss (not analysed here).
alpha-suffix averaging is a paper-A-specific construction tied to its convergence-rate analysis; nothing in paper B corresponds.
Bounded second moment of a stochastic subgradient oracle is a SGD-analysis assumption; paper B has no such oracle.

Projected SGD with eta_t=1/(lambda t) is the algorithm under analysis in paper A. Paper B's algorithm AP13.1 (Conditional Flow Matching training) is a regression-loss minimisation for a neural vector field; despite both being iterative, they solve disjoint problems with disjoint update rules. Cross-type/cross-problem match would have no mathematical content.
SVM regularised hinge-loss objective is an experimental instance in paper A; no analogue in paper B.

Last-iterate O(1/T) rate for smooth strongly convex SGD has no counterpart in paper B, which proves identities about generators of probability paths and gradient equivalence of FM/CFM losses, not optimisation rates.
Distance-decay lemma E||w_T-w*||^2 <= 4G^2/(lambda^2 T) is intrinsic to the SGD recurrence analysis; paper B has no such iterate-distance bound.
O(1/T) rate for the average iterate in the smooth case is a paper-A optimisation theorem with no counterpart in paper B.
Omega(log T/T) lower bound for SGD-average on a non-smooth boundary instance; paper B proves no lower bounds and has no notion of optimisation rate over T iterations.
Interior-optimum Omega(log T/T) lower bound; same reasoning as TP8.3 — no analogue.
O(1/T) upper bound for alpha-suffix averaging; no counterpart in paper B.
High-probability iterate-distance bound via Freedman; paper B has no high-probability bounds.
Initial-distance bound E||w_1-w*||^2 <= 4G^2/lambda^2 from strong convexity; no analogue in paper B.
Maximal Freedman-style martingale bound; no martingale concentration appears in paper B.
One-sided constraint lemma for the non-smooth lower-bound instance; no analogue in paper B.
Almost-sure uniform iterate-distance bound for SGD; no analogue.
Recursive-form decomposition unrolling SGD into a martingale sum; no analogue in paper B's identity-based proofs.
Proof of LP8.1 via strong-convexity recurrence and induction on 1/t; the proof technique (recurrence on E||w_t-w*||^2) has no analogue in paper B.
Proof of TP8.2 via Cauchy-Schwartz on cross terms and induction; no analogue.
Lower-bound proof via case split on Z_t and conditional expectation; no analogue.
Lower-bound proof using the non-consecutive-zero indicator argument; no analogue.
Suffix-averaging proof summing the per-step recurrence; no analogue.
High-probability proof combining Freedman's inequality with the recursive decomposition and quadratic induction; no analogue in paper B.
Open problem about last-iterate rate for non-smooth strongly convex SGD; not addressed by paper B.
Probability density path p:[0,1]xR^d->R is a generative-modelling object with no counterpart in paper A's optimisation setting.
Time-dependent vector field v_t(x) is the central object of flow matching; paper A has no continuous-time vector fields.
Diffeomorphic flow phi_t generated by an ODE; paper A's iterates are discrete-time and not diffeomorphic flows.
Push-forward of densities by a diffeomorphism; no analogue in paper A.
Generation of a probability path by a vector field; foreign to paper A.
Conditional probability path p_t(x|x_1); no analogue.
Marginal probability path as mixture of conditional paths; no analogue.
Marginal vector field formula; foreign to paper A.
Gaussian conditional probability path with mean mu_t and std sigma_t; no analogue.
Affine conditional Gaussian flow psi_t; no analogue.

Flow Matching loss L_FM = E||v_t - u_t||^2 is a regression loss for a neural vector field; paper A's only loss is the suboptimality F(w)-F(w*) and the SVM hinge loss in experiments. The two losses share no structure.
Conditional Flow Matching loss; paper-B-specific.
VE conditional vector field; no analogue.
VP conditional vector field; no analogue.
OT conditional vector field; no analogue.
CFM loss specialised to OT path; no analogue.
Theorem that the marginal vector field generates the marginal probability path is a continuity-equation identity; paper A has no PDE-level statements.

Equivalence of FM and CFM gradients (as theta-gradients of regression losses) is a paper-B-specific identity. Although paper A also reasons about gradients, those are stochastic subgradients of F and the analysis is operator-level (recurrences on E||.||^2), not gradient-of-loss-equivalence.
Closed-form Gaussian conditional vector field; no analogue.
Time-reversal of vector fields (continuous-time); no analogue.

CFM training algorithm minimises a regression loss over neural-network parameters using arbitrary stochastic gradient methods; paper A's SGD analyses convergence on a strongly convex F, not training of a regression model. The algorithms inhabit different problem worlds.
Simulation-free CNF training problem; paper A's problem of strongly-convex stochastic optimisation does not subsume or correspond to it.
Continuity-equation verification via Leibniz rule; no analogous proof technique in paper A.
Proof of FM/CFM gradient equivalence via Fubini and bilinearity of the inner product; paper A's proofs operate on iterate-distance recurrences.
Closed-form derivation of u_t via inversion of the affine flow; no analogue.
Time-reversal proof for vector fields; no analogue.
